message.abstract:
<jats:p><jats:italic>Context.</jats:italic> The multiplicity fraction of stars, down to the substellar regime, is a parameter of fundamental importance for stellar formation, evolution, and planetology. The census of multiple stars in the solar neighborhood is however incomplete.</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Aims.</jats:italic> Our study is aimed at detecting companions of H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc> catalog stars from the proper motion anomaly (PMa) they induce on their host star, namely, the difference between their long-term H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc>-<jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> and short-term <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> proper motion vectors. We also aim to detect resolved, gravitationally bound companions of the H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc> catalog stars (117 955 stars) and of the <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> EDR3 stars closer than 100 pc (542 232 stars).</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Methods.</jats:italic> Using the H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc> and EDR3 data, we revised the PMa catalog for the H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc> stars. In order to identify gravitationally bound visual companions of our sample, we searched the <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> EDR3 catalog for common proper-motion (CPM) candidates.</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Results.</jats:italic> The detection of tangential velocity anomalies with a median accuracy of <jats:italic>σ</jats:italic>(Δ<jats:italic>v</jats:italic><jats:sub>T</jats:sub>) = 26 cm s<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> per parsec of distance is demonstrated with the EDR3. This improvement by a factor 2.5 in accuracy, as compared to <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> DR2, results in PMa detection limits on companions that are well into the planetary mass regime for many targets. We identify 37 515 H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc> stars presenting a PMa at significant level (<jats:italic>S</jats:italic>/<jats:italic>N</jats:italic> > 3), namely, a fraction of 32% (compared to 30% for the DR2) and 12 914 (11%) hosting CPM bound candidate companions. After including the <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> EDR3 renormalised unit weight error (RUWE > 1.4) as an additional indicator, 50 720 stars of the H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc> catalog (43%) exhibit at least one signal of binarity. Among the <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> EDR3 stars located within 100 pc, we find CPM bound candidate companions for 39 490 stars (7.3% of the sample).</jats:p>
<jats:p><jats:italic>Conclusions.</jats:italic> The search for companions using a combination of the PMa, CPM, and RUWE indicators significantly improves the exhaustivity of the multiplicity survey. The detection of CPM companions of very bright stars (heavily saturated on the <jats:italic>Gaia</jats:italic> detectors) that are classical benchmark objects for stellar physics provides a useful proxy for estimating their distance with a higher accuracy than with H<jats:sc>IPPARCOS</jats:sc>.</jats:p>
title: Stellar and substellar companions from Gaia EDR3
